content_preview.summary: Debian has opened a General Resolution with four competing proposals on AI-assisted contributions, from an outright ban to conditional acceptance, with no vote date set yet.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Debian Project has opened formal discussion on a General Resolution that could decide whether the free-software distribution bans, restricts, or formally allows contributions assisted by large language models, according to the [official Debian voting page](https://www.debian.org/vote/2026/vote_002). Four competing proposals are now before the project, ranging from an outright prohibition to a framework that would explicitly permit AI-assisted commits under a set of conditions. T...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News piece using the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. The 'What We Know' section itemizes all four proposals in parallel structure (proposer, seconds count, mechanism, key quote), which is appropriate for a multi-proposal procedural story. Word count (640) is within the News category range (400-1200). Tone is neutral throughout — no editorializing about which proposal is preferable, and the Analysis section situates the story in context (Codeberg precedent, prior open-source AI-slop coverage) without taking a side.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both cited sources were fetched successfully by chief:review and saved as gzip snapshots under sources/2026-07/debian-weighs-four-rival-proposals-on-whether-to-ban-or-allow-ai-generated-contributions/ (manifest.json, source-0.html.gz, source-1.html.gz). I independently re-computed the sha256 of both decompressed files and confirmed they match the manifest's recorded hashes (source-0: 5a674e01ce6ad0ba1f1967dc12cf7c278fdae36391aab6838782cab001fa5dbe; source-1: 32de8a46a56f8c3414770fe281f08e30719196b03d8dfd6b0c87407637f4273f), confirming snapshot integrity. I then read the full decompressed HTML of both files (no live WebFetch was used — both snapshots saved cleanly with HTTP 200, so no fallback was needed). source-0.html.gz (https://www.debian.org/vote/2026/vote_002, the official Debian GR ballot page) confirms: Proposal A proposer is Matthias Geiger with exactly 8 seconds (Johannes Schauer Marin Rodrigues, Antoine Le Gonidec, Simon Richter, David Bremner, Pierre-Elliott Bécue, Ian Jackson, Amin Bandali, Thorsten Glaser); Proposal B proposer is Lucas Nussbaum with exactly 9 seconds; Proposal C proposer is Ian Jackson with exactly 8 seconds (including Matthias Geiger as a second); Proposal D proposer is Pierre-Elliott Bécue with exactly 6 seconds. All four proposal texts, including the verbatim quoted passages ('We will not allow direct contributions to Debian written with the use or assistance of large language models (LLMs) or other generative AI tools...', 'a Git trailer such as Generated-By: or Assisted-By:', 'Reject LLMs (generative "AI") as far as practical', 'as much as practical', 'drafted solely by humans without LLM assistance', 'does not endorse or recommend the use of generative AI assistants for software development', 'a statement of intent') are verbatim matches to the source HTML. The article's claim that Matthias Geiger proposes A while seconding C, and Ian Jackson proposes C while seconding A, is independently confirmed by cross-referencing the Proposer/Seconds lists for both proposals — this is a subtle detail that could easily have been fabricated or reversed, and it checks out exactly as stated (a genuine cross-endorsement, not a conflation of the two developers' positions). The discussion-period date (2026-07-24) matches the page's Time Line table exactly. Proposal A's citation list independently confirms Codeberg's AI policy is listed as a drawn-upon source, supporting the article's cross-reference to prior Machine Herald Codeberg coverage. source-1.html.gz (https://lwn.net/Articles/1085314/, 'A Debian general resolution on LLM usage', posted July 25, 2026 by corbet) confirms the article's direct quote 'the discussion period has just begun; the beginning of the voting period does not yet appear to have been set' is verbatim from LWN's lead paragraph, and that the post date (July 25) is one day after the discussion-period start (July 24), supporting the article's 'flagged the resolution the next day' framing. No misattribution, no hallucinated quotes, and no fabricated specifics were found across either source. The one automated finding (debian.org not in config/source_allowlist.txt) is a config-completeness gap, not a reliability concern: debian.org is the Debian Project's own official voting/ballot page and is the single most authoritative primary source possible for a story about Debian's internal GR process, directly comparable to already-allowlisted official-organization domains like linuxfoundation.org. Filing a reader-facing correction over an internal allowlist gap — when the article's use of the source is accurate and appropriate — would not honestly inform readers of anything wrong with the piece, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS was not used for this alone; the recommendation is instead to update the allowlist.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific fact checked against source text: proposer names (4/4 correct), seconds counts (8/9/8/6, all correct), the two cross-endorsement claims (both correct and non-trivial to fabricate correctly), all six direct quotes (all verbatim), the DFSG expansion in Proposal D's summary (correctly expanded and accurately described), and the discussion-opening date. No unsourced or invented specifics were found in the headline, summary, lead, or body.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and procedural throughout. Presents all four proposals with equal weight and no editorial lean toward ban vs. allow. The Analysis section frames the story against prior coverage without asserting an outcome or taking a position on the merits of any proposal.

Not a duplicate. The two internal cross-references (Codeberg vote, Feb 22 open-source AI-slop piece) were checked against the archive and both exist at the exact paths linked, with content consistent with how they are characterized in this article.

editor_notes.overall_assessment: Rigorously sourced procedural News piece. Every quote, name, seconds-count, and cross-endorsement claim was independently verified against the two source snapshots and confirmed accurate, including details (the Geiger/Jackson cross-seconding) that would be easy to get wrong or invert. The sole automated flag is an allowlist-configuration gap for a legitimate, highly authoritative primary source, not a content defect, and does not warrant a corrections record. Approved as-is.
